To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new class of palladium complexes with a tetradentate ligand, Pd3, is developed and characterized.

a tetradentate palladium-based phosphorscent excimer complex, Pd(III)3O3, is synthesized and characterized and used to demonstrate highly efficient, stable, and efficient single-doped white organic light-emitting diodes (WOLEDs) using a stable device design.

the tetradentate palladium complex, Pd 3O3, is synthesized and characterized, and it is used in single-doped phosphorescent white organic light-emitting devices (W-OLEDs) with high efficiency and long lifetime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new phosphorescent emitters and their use in OLEDs.
the design and synthesis of a new class of stable and efficient single-doped white emitting phosphorescent materials.
the design, synthesis, and application of a new class of stable phosphorescent emitters for OLEDs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a new class of stable blue excimer emitter is developed, and the first stable warm white OLEDs based on excimers are developed.
the palladium based complex, Pd 3 O 3, can achieve high efficiency and stability in a white OLEDs with a peak external quantum efficiency of 27.2% and a power efficiency of 81 Lm W-1.
Pd3O 3 has demonstrated the highest performance for a stable white OLEDs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pd3O 3 can be used in stable white OLEDs with high efficiency.
we synthesized a new class of stable blue and white phosphorescent excimers based on a tetradentate palladium complex, Pd 3 O 3, which is the only palladium based excimer to date.
Pd3O2 and Pd3O4 complexes are synthesized and characterized, and Pd3 complexes are found to be efficient and stable blue emitters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the excimer based OLEDs using Pd3O2 complexes can achieve high efficiency, stability, and color tunability, and are a good alternative to Pt-based OLEDs.
Pd complexes are an excellent alternative to Pt complexes in excimer based stable OLEDs.
Pd3O-based phosphorescent complexes can be used as efficient blue emitters and can be used as stable and highly efficient excimer-based white emitters.
